# `ota_get_session`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater (firmware 9.75): read the state of the current OTA session.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ (firmware 9.75) |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, updater RPC handler @0x26500 and GetSession @0x35ad0 (64-bit build), OTA manager; 32-bit GetSession @0x3693c; app 3.3.2 OtaService DTOs |

Firmware 9.75 (app 3.4.0) registers this method in the updater on TCP 4350, in both the 64-bit and 32-bit builds; firmware 9.31 registered none of the OTA methods (its updater had four). The handler clears the thread error code and calls the updater's single OTA manager. The OTA methods do not use the imager/guider secure-session layer (no such code in the updater); whether the JSON on 4350 is wrapped is not established. Firmware update is a high-risk operation; do not send this to a real device to test it. Replies with the session stage and the modules received so far (firmware 9.75, 64-bit build, READ). The members are stage, target_main_version for a non-idle session, received_modules, receiving_module (an array of entries with name, version and sha256, populated conditionally), missing_modules and, after a failure, a failure object with stage, an optional module, an integer code and error text. Members by stage (firmware 9.75, 64-bit build, READ). idle gives stage and received_modules. pending and receiving give stage, target_main_version, received_modules, receiving_module and missing_modules. upgrading gives stage, target_main_version and received_modules. complete gives stage and target_main_version only. fail gives stage and target_main_version, then failure when the failure flag is set, then received_modules, receiving_module and missing_modules. So one schema with every member always present is wrong. The receiving_module array holds one object with name, version and sha256 when a receiving module is set and found, otherwise it is empty (at most one element is INFERRED). The 32-bit build was not compared member by member. When module is present inside failure, and the entry shape of missing_modules, are unresolved. The app continues a new upgrade only when the stage is blank, idle, fail or complete. The stage after each received module is INFERRED to be receiving.

Side effects: None.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"ota_get_session"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read by the handler. The app omits it. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ (app 3.3.2 emitter); firmware handler reads no params INFERRED] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Request, request - App shape; params omitted (READ):

```json
{"id":100,"method":"ota_get_session"}
```

Reply, ok - Shape READ; values invented; member presence INFERRED:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"ota_get_session","result":{"stage":"idle","received_modules":[],"target_main_version":"9.99"},"code":0,"id":100}
```
